LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 6.1.1 CONVERSATIONAL SKILLS: DISAGREEING POLITELY

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.1: Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Conversational Skills: Disagreeing Politely
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Conversational Skills: Disagreeing Politely, part of Strand 6 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 8 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: where characters agree or disagree politely. ● In small groups, guide the learners to write a short dialogue 1. Why should people disagree appropriately?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. list ways of disagreeing politely,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Conversational Skills: Disagreeing Politely in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use conversational strategies to disagree appropriately,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Conversational Skills: Disagreeing Politely in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. apply non-verbal cues to express varied moods and feelings,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Conversational Skills: Disagreeing Politely in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. advocate for the need to speak politely during communication. ● Guide the learners with low vision to watch and learners with blindness listen to a short audio- visual or read an excerpt in which speakers disagree appropriately and identify polite expressions used. ● In pairs, guide the learners to role play the events depicted in the audio-visual or excerpt. ● In pairs, guide the learners to practise disagreeing politely while incorporating non-verbal cues. ● Guide the learners to listen to a dialogue where characters agree or disagree politely. ● In small groups, guide the learners to write a short dialogue 1. A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Conversational Skills: Disagreeing Politely together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

appropriate language and tone to disagree politely.
